data.name: Ammat
data.long_meaning: The name Ammat is derived from the Arabic root 'amata', which means 'to inform, to remember, or to support'. In Islamic tradition, Ammat refers to the mothers of believers, and is a term of respect and honor for women who nurture and support their families and communities.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with deep spiritual significance, Ammat is also associated with the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) beloved wife, Aisha (ra), who was known for her dedication to her husband and her community.

in_arabic.name: أمات
in_arabic.meaning: أمات تعني أم أو مربية أو خادمة في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أمات هو اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي و يعني أم أو مربية أو خادمة. وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في القرآن الكريم في سورة الإسراء الآية 31: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق ۚ نحن نرزقهم ولكم

in_urdu.name: اماٹ
in_urdu.meaning: اماٹ کا مطلب ہے ماں یا مربی یا خادمہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: اماٹ ایک علم مؤنث نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے ماں یا مربی یا خادمہ۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں مقبول ہے

in_hindi.name: अमाट
in_hindi.meaning: अमाट का अर्थ है माता या पालनहार या सेविका
in_hindi.long_meaning: अमाट एक स्त्रीलिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है माता या पालनहार या सेविका। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में प्रयोग किया जाता है

in_pashto.name: اماټ
in_pashto.meaning: اماټ د مور یا پالونکې یا خدمتګارې معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: اماټ د ښځینه علم نوم دی چی د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستی دی. دا د مور یا پالونکې یا خدمتګارې معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ټولنو کې کارول کیږي

in_english.name: Ammat

data.cultural_impact: The name Ammat carries a deep cultural significance in Islamic societies, as it is a term of reverence and appreciation for mothers. The Arabic root 'amata' connotes the idea of informing, remembering, and supporting, which are essential roles of a mother. By giving this name to their children, parents express their gratitude and respect for the vital role that mothers play in shaping their lives and upholding the values of the Islamic community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ammat also holds a spiritual significance, as it represents the Islamic virtue of compassion and nurturing. Mothers are considered a source of comfort and guidance, and the nurturing they provide to their children is seen as a reflection of the divine mercy and compassion of God. Furthermore, the term Ammat also reminds us of the critical role that mothers play in transmitting the Islamic faith to future generations. By upholding their spiritual and ethical responsibilities as mothers, women contribute to the continuity and vitality of the Islamic community, and strengthen the bonds of faith and belonging among its members.
